body:
The maintainer asked on 2026-11-20 if the browser build should also lose its hardcoded list and read from disk.

Decision (recommended, taken): yes. The `include_str!` copy is removed from the browser build too. A browser page cannot read a disk folder: the File System Access API exists only in Chromium browsers and asks for the folder in each session. So the browser build reads the same folders from the web server.

Plan for the browser build:
- The site build already serves `assets/posts` and `assets/machines` from the tagged tree. The page fetches the files from its own origin at start-up.
- The site build writes a manifest that lists the files of each folder. No Rust list names a file.
- A user can add a post file or a machine file with an upload. This is optional and can be a sub-issue.
- The first start needs the network. A failed fetch gives a refusal by name, not an empty list.
- The wasm binary gets smaller. The 63 compiled-in files leave it.

This replaces the line "if this is too large, split it out and keep the list for the browser build". The browser part can be a sub-issue of #2949, but it is part of the done condition: no `include_str!` of a post or machine file remains in `crates/app/src`.

Check in the work: the manifest step is in `release.yml` or `site/` without a new trigger (AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted").

The browser build needs a way to load the maintainer's own machine and post files from his disk. This is tracked in #2950. The browser part of this issue depends on #2950: the compiled-in copy is removed only when the browser loads files by fetch (the site folder) and by the picker or drop (the user's disk).

Escalation by Codex (skull), before a claim. I made no code change and pushed no branch.

This work is larger than `effort:high`. I raise the label to `effort:max`. These are the reasons:

- The issue asks for an open design. A file must state its display name, its sort order and its default role. This is a new header in each `.cps` and `.mch` file, or a new index file format. The table in AGENTS.md puts "formats or open design" in `effort:max`.
- The tables have about 70 call sites on upstream/main `aa4c785db`:
  - `crates/app/src`: `posting.rs` (lines 128, 253-301, 433-444), `posting_offer.rs:47`, `posting_serves.rs:50`, `commands/post.rs:55`, `commands/post_script_options.rs:58`, `machine/fields.rs:111`, `machine/library.rs:122-247`, `machine/validate.rs:385`, `mcp/setup_tools.rs:273-330`, `mcp/tools.rs:389`.
  - `crates/ui/src`: `machine_page.rs:61`, `post_pick.rs:33`, `machine_modes.rs`, and three structural tests.
  - About 40 files in `crates/app/tests/`, and `crates/post/tests/folder_scan.rs`.
- Many call sites use `&'static str` names: `FolderScan::present`, `LATHE_POSTS`, `WIRE_POSTS`, `SINKER_POSTS`, `PLASMA_POSTS` and the `POST_TEXT` and `MACHINE_TEXT` cells, which are indexed by table position. Names that come from a disk file at run time are not `'static`, and they can change at each `rescan`. A new ownership model is necessary. A leaked string for each rescan is not permitted (AGENTS.md: "A leak is a critical bug").
- The role lists (`LATHE_POSTS` and the others in `posting_serves.rs`) name posts by registry name. The issue wants the role to come from the file. This changes which posts the app offers for a machine kind. This is under the safety floor.
- The browser part depends on #2950, which is open. The done condition says that no `include_str!` of a post or machine file stays in `crates/app/src`.

Recommended split (the next worker can take or change it):

1. Design and header format. Add a header line to each shipped file, for example `// camcraft: name="Fanuc" order=0 role=mill`. Add a parser in `camcraft_post::data_scan` that returns owned names. Add a test that every file in `assets/posts` and `assets/machines` has a valid header. Add a test that the header name of each file is the same as its old table name.
2. Alias map and resolution. Add `posting_alias.rs`, which maps each old registry name to its file name. Add the safety test: each old name resolves to the same file as before, and a missing file is refused by name. `PostRef::Builtin` resolves to `fanuc.cps`.
3. Migrate the call sites to an owned registry, for example `Arc<[Entry]>` that is replaced at each rescan. Delete `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES`. Tests read the folders.
4. Browser build: a site manifest and fetch at start-up, after #2950.

Note by Codex (skull). I did not claim this issue. I made no code change.

This issue cannot be done in one PR now. These are the reasons:

- The done condition says that no `include_str!` of a post or machine file stays in `crates/app/src`. The browser part depends on #2950. The PR for #2950 is #3160. It is a draft and is not merged.
- The tables have about 87 references in `crates/` on upstream/main `a35c9cb81`. The migration needs a new ownership model for the names (see the comment above). This is under the safety floor.

Recommendation: file the four parts of the split in the comment above as sub-issues. Each part is one PR with `Refs #2949`. Part 4 (browser build) waits for #3160. Then this umbrella closes with the last part.

Until the sub-issues exist, a worker cannot finish this issue with `Fixes #2949`.

Note by an issue worker (Opus). I did not claim this issue. I made no code change.

Status on upstream/main `ec314174e`:

- The browser dependency is clear. #2950 is closed, and its PR #3160 merged on 2026-11-22.
- `BUILTINS` (line 36) and `MACHINES` (line 92) are still in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. The file has 450 lines.
- `posting_files.rs` has 78 `include_str!` lines for post and machine files. The count was 63 when the issue was filed.
- The tables and the two text readers have 196 references in 96 files under `crates/`.

The work is still too large for one PR with `Fixes #2949`. The scope grows each week.

Recommendation: file the four parts of the split in the escalation comment as sub-issues now. Part 4 (browser build) is no longer blocked. Each part is one PR with `Refs #2949`. The last part closes this issue. Until the sub-issues exist, a worker cannot take this issue.
